key_insight: MANTRA will test whether early angiotensin-II therapy normalizes renin–angiotensin–aldosterone system abnormalities and modulates innate immune responses in septic shock.
clinical_relevance: This septic shock study—not AI or cancer drug discovery—may clarify biological differences between angiotensin-II and norepinephrine treatment strategies.
method: Prospective, multicenter, open-label randomized mechanistic trial targeting 78 adults with septic shock.
Participants receive a primary angiotensin-II or norepinephrine strategy for 48 hours, allocated 1:1.
Primary analysis compares plasma renin trajectories from baseline to 24 hours; secondary measures assess immune biology, organ support, and safety.
evidence_signal: The protocol reports 90% power to detect a 25% between-group difference in 24-hour renin at a two-sided alpha of 0.05; no trial results are reported.
watch_item: The small, open-label mechanistic design cannot by itself establish improved survival or other patient-centered benefits.
paper_title: Mechanistic Assessment of Norepinephrine Therapy versus Angiotensin-II on Organ Function in Septic Shock (MANTRA): Study Protocol for a multicenter open-label randomized trial
